findings.text: The first lines tell a newcomer what Athena is and what this page is: a study of another project that shows Athena can explain unfamiliar code, with every statement traced to a source.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository.

findings.text: The 'Start here' section works well. It says what firstmate is, follows one task from start to finish in numbered steps, and lists the failure cases. A newcomer gets the main points before the detailed state and transition sections.
The page ends with clear next steps. It links to Athena's repository for install and trial, links to firstmate, and explains how to check a claim. A newcomer knows what to do next.
Several terms are used but never defined, including 'unheld', 'backlog gate' and 'endpoint'. 'Unheld' already appears in the 'Start here' steps, so a newcomer meets it before any explanation.
findings.source: Under the backlog gate, dispatch accepts only an unheld, unblocked Queued or In flight item

findings.text: The glossary defines 'ship' only by pointing to 'scouts', which is never defined. 'home' is also undefined in 'backlog item': "A unit of work in a home's backlog". These gaps weaken the glossary just where a newcomer would look for help.
findings.source: glossary entry 'ship': A kind of task, named next to scouts.

findings.text: Most of the page is about firstmate's internals, not about Athena. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena has to work out from the lede that the firstmate detail is a demonstration. One sentence on why a firstmate user would care could help readers who came for firstmate.
findings.source: Athena explains how firstmate handles work

findings.text: Two claims list the same source link twice. This is minor, but it looks like a mistake on a page that is meant to show careful citation.
findings.source: claim-c2 sources: docs/configuration.md:357-357 listed twice; claim-c14: bin/fm-teardown.sh:22-23 listed twice

findings.text: The page is honest that nothing was run and every claim comes from reading the files. It does not say this in the opening, though, so a newcomer only learns about the limits near the end.
findings.source: Limits of this study — f1: "no failure or retry edge was observed; every claim is marked read"
